subject: Re: DPA — purge/playbook timeline, onshore access & evidence
messages:
From: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@aurorahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Systems Legal <legal@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: DPA: retention & purge timeline Qs

Vanessa — thanks again for the call earlier. Two quick follow-ups from our legal and security teams as we prepare the DPA redlines:

1) Purge timeline: for subject erasure requests we need confirmation that primary processing data and any backups can be purged within 30 days of effective erasure. Are there carve-outs for disaster-recovery snapshots or cold backups, and if so what is the maximum hold?

2) Onshore access logs: our compliance team wants a description of how you provide evidence of onshore access (audit logs showing which engineers or support personnel accessed data and from which region). They also asked whether Redwood stores any cross-border admin logs for routing/fallthrough events.

3) Evidence: would you be able to provide an erase certificate template and a short playbook showing the steps you run for an erasure that covers primary, cache, and any KV caches used by inference?

We want to avoid a long negotiation; if you can propose concrete redline language for the DPA that addresses (1)-(3) we can run it by our counsel.

Appreciate a quick turnaround this week.

— Sara
Director, Procurement
Aurora Health Systems
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: retention & purge timeline Qs

Sara — thanks, and glad we could talk through the high level. I pulled together a proposed package to keep reviews tight: 1) suggested DPA clause wording (see attachment Aurora_DPA_redlines_v2.docx), 2) an erase-cert template (erase-cert-template.pdf) and 3) a short onshore-access playbook in spreadsheet form with sample log fields (onshore-access-log-playbook.xlsx).

Short answers inline here so your team can triage immediately: 
- Purge timeline: Our standard: primary data and hot caches are removed within 30 days of validated erasure. Backups/snapshots are typically rotated/retained up to 90 days; however we can commit to a maximum backup retention of 90 days unless mutually agreed exceptions apply (e.g., legal hold). We include an explicit paragraph that backups are subject to reasonable recovery windows and will be purged at the next scheduled rotation within 90 days.
- Onshore access logs: We produce audit logs that record account, action, timestamp, source IP (VPC range), and region tag. For Private deployments we can provide proof of in-region admin access only. For Hosted accounts we record cross-region operator activity in our audit system and can export a filtered view scoped to your tenant for a given period.
- Evidence/playbook: Attached erase certificate template and playbook. The playbook documents the steps to invalidate keys, flush runtime caches (including KV cache), delete application-level artifacts, and trigger evidence capture.

Next steps I propose: Laura (legal) and Rishi (infra) below will propose precise redline language and a short amendment you can share with counsel. If that looks good we can send via DocuSign and attach the erase cert as schedule. I can also schedule a 30-minute call with your security folks to walk the playbook.

Action: can you confirm whether Aurora requires the 30-day purge for both Hosted + Dedicated, or only for on-prem/Private deployments? That will affect the redline scope.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Head of G&A Sales, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 11:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA: retention & purge timeline Qs

Sara / Vanessa — looping in a couple technical/contractual clarifications and an initial redline suggestion.

On scope: If Aurora insists on a firm 30-day wipe for backups in hosted environments, we need to be explicit about exceptions for (a) disaster recovery snapshots that are immutable for short windows and (b) instances where backups are encrypted with a customer-managed key and cannot be retroactively altered without the keyholder. Our suggested trade: commit to 30 days for primary data and hot caches; commit to purge-from-backup-within-90-days except where immutable snapshot policy applies — in those cases Redwood will provide documented rotation windows and reasonable steps to expedite if Aurora supplies the KEK.

Suggested DPA clause (for your counsel to consider): "Redwood will erase Customer Data from primary production stores and runtime caches within thirty (30) days following Customer's validated erasure request. Backups and archived snapshots will be deleted within ninety (90) days of the erasure request; provided that immutable recovery snapshots that cannot be programmatically altered are excluded and will be retained only for the remaining snapshot retention period, and Redwood will provide the Customer with written notice and documented rotation schedule for such snapshots. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood will cooperate with Customer and, where feasible, execute expedited deletion steps if Customer provides the encryption key controlling the snapshot."

On logs/evidence: We propose an appendix describing the log fields we can export and the standard retention for audit logs (default 365 days in hosted; configurable in Dedicated). We will also add an erase-certificate template to the DPA as a schedule.

If that language looks acceptable in principle I can turn it into tracked changes for your counsel this afternoon.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@aurorahealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora Health Systems Legal <legal@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA: retention & purge timeline Qs

Thanks Laura — that draft helps. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after reading the proposed clause: 

• For the backup exception where snapshots are immutable: can Redwood provide a documented runbook that shows the snapshot rotation cadence and who owns the snapshot lifecycle? That needs to be part of our evidence package.

• On the customer-supplied key path: Aurora needs confirmation that if we supply a KEK to enable expedited deletion, Redwood will not persist or retain a copy of that key after the deletion action is completed.

• Logs: we need the sample export (CSV/JSON) you referenced so our compliance team can validate fields. The playbook spreadsheet is fine but our auditors prefer a one-page sample output.

If you can commit to the three items above and provide the one-page sample export we can likely accept the clause and proceed to signature. We can also do the 30-minute technical walk-through after we confirm the sample export is sufficient.

— Sara
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.mendez@aurorahealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Apr 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: retention & purge timeline Qs

Sara — thanks for the precise asks. Quick commitments from infra side and next actions below.

1) Snapshot runbook: attached is a short runbook and the rotation cadence we use for Aurora's intended region (US-East region snapshots rotate on a 7–14 day cadence; immutable snapshots are flagged and have a documented expiration). We will include this as an appendix to the DPA.

2) Customer KEK path: If Aurora elects to provide a customer-managed key to enable expedited deletion, Redwood will use the key only for the purpose set out in the DPA and will not persist a copy of the key. After deletion actions are complete Redwood will zeroize any transient copies and confirm by certificate (we will add language to the erase-certificate template to reflect zeroization and timestamp).

3) Sample export: I've attached a one-page sample JSON export showing audit fields: timestamp, user_id, action, resource_id, source_ip, region_tag. We'll produce the CSV/JSON equivalent for any requested window as part of evidence.

Next steps: Laura, can you incorporate Rishi's two short sentences about KEK zeroization and snapshot appendix into the final tracked redline? Vanessa, I suggest we send the updated redline with attachments to Aurora legal via DocuSign and include the erase-cert as schedule A. I'll coordinate the security walk-through once we have their preferred window.

Attachments (stubs): onshore-access-log-playbook.xlsx; erase-cert-template.pdf; Aurora_DPA_redlines_v2.docx

— Rishi Malhotra
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability, Redwood Inference
